summary: This experimental RFC specifies signaling of additional Segment Routing Segment Types for SR Policies in BGP using the SR Policy SAFI.

plainLanguage.summary: Segment Routing lets a controller list the exact steps a packet should take through the network. This RFC finishes the job of letting BGP carry that list, by defining how to encode the remaining kinds of step, such as a node address, a specific interface, or a particular link between two routers.

subtitle: Encoding every Segment Routing segment type inside a BGP SR Policy.

tldr.problem: The BGP SR Policy address family defined the encoding for only two of the eleven segment types in the Segment Routing architecture, so a controller could not advertise the other nine.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC defines a Segment sub-TLV for each remaining type, from Type C through Type K, each carrying node addresses, interface identifiers or adjacency addresses, plus optional algorithm and SID fields.
tldr.outcome: The new sub-TLVs carry no new operations and introduce no new security considerations; they reuse the security and manageability rules of the parent document.

facts.label: Type C length
facts.value: 10 octets with the SR-MPLS SID, 6 without

facts.label: Type G length
facts.value: 46 octets with the SR-MPLS SID, 42 without

facts.label: New flag bits
facts.value: Bit 1 the A-Flag, bit 2 the S-Flag

today: RFC 9831 is an Experimental RFC and has not been obsoleted or updated. It is a companion to RFC 9830, whose security and manageability considerations it inherits unchanged, and it adds no new operations or fault management behaviour of its own.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The BGP Segment Routing Policy Subsequent Address Family Identifier was introduced by RFC 9830 for the advertisement of SR Policies (RFC 8402). RFC 9830 introduced the base SR Segment Types A and B, as specified by the SR Policy Architecture (RFC 9256).

This document specifies the extensions for the advertisement of the remaining SR Segment Types defined in RFC 9256 in the SR Policy SAFI, for both SR-MPLS (see RFC 8660) and Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) (see RFC 8754 and RFC 8986).

The extensions do not impact the SR Policy operations or fault management as specified in RFC 9830. Validation of an explicit path encoded by the Segment List sub-TLV is beyond the scope of BGP and is performed by the Segment Routing Policy Module as described in RFC 9830. As specified in the architecture, a mix of SR-MPLS and SRv6 segments makes the segment list invalid.
sections.plainLanguage: Segment Routing lets a controller list the exact steps a packet should take through the network. This RFC finishes the job of letting BGP carry that list, by defining how to encode the remaining kinds of step, such as a node address, a specific interface, or a particular link between two routers.

sections.title: The Segment Types
sections.content:
The Segment List sub-TLV of RFC 9830 encodes a single explicit path towards the endpoint. It includes the elements of the path, that is, the segments. A Segment sub-TLV describes a single segment in a segment list, that is, a single element of the explicit path.

Section 4 of RFC 9256 defines several Segment Types for SR-MPLS and SRv6:

  • Type A: SR-MPLS Label
  • Type B: SRv6 SID
  • Type C: IPv4 Prefix with optional SR Algorithm
  • Type D: IPv6 Global Prefix with optional SR Algorithm for SR-MPLS
  • Type E: IPv4 Prefix with Local Interface ID
  • Type F: IPv4 Addresses for link endpoints as Local, Remote pair
  • Type G: IPv6 Prefix and Interface ID for link endpoints as Local, Remote pair for SR-MPLS
  • Type H: IPv6 Addresses for link endpoints as Local, Remote pair for SR-MPLS
  • Type I: IPv6 Global Prefix with optional SR Algorithm for SRv6
  • Type J: IPv6 Prefix and Interface ID for link endpoints as Local, Remote pair for SRv6
  • Type K: IPv6 Addresses for link endpoints as Local, Remote pair for SRv6

RFC 9830 specifies the Segment Type Sub-TLVs for Types A and B. This document specifies the sub-TLVs for each of the others. The nine new types fall into three groups. Types C, D and I name a node by its address, optionally with an SR Algorithm and a segment identifier. Types E, G and J name a node by its address together with a local interface identifier, which pins the step to one of the node's interfaces. Types F, H and K name a link by giving the local and remote addresses at its two ends.
sections.plainLanguage: There are eleven kinds of step. Two were already defined: a plain MPLS label and an SRv6 identifier. The other nine are added here, in three families: steps that name a router, steps that name a router and one of its interfaces, and steps that name the link between two routers.

sections.title: Encoding a Segment That Names a Node
sections.content:
Every Segment Type sub-TLV starts the same way. The first octet is the Type, and the second is the Length, which specifies the length of the value field, not including the Type and Length fields, in octets. The third octet is a Flags field, and the fourth is either an SR Algorithm or a reserved octet.

The Type C sub-TLV has Type 3 and encodes an IPv4 node address, an SR Algorithm and an optional SR-MPLS Segment Identifier. The Length MUST be 10 when the SR-MPLS SID is present and 6 otherwise. The IPv4 Node Address is a 4-octet address representing a node. The optional SR-MPLS SID is a 4-octet field containing a label, Traffic Class, bottom-of-stack and TTL, as defined for Segment Type A.

The Type D sub-TLV has Type 4 and does the same for IPv6. The Length MUST be 22 when the SR-MPLS SID is present and 18 otherwise, and the IPv6 Node Address is 16 octets.

The Type I sub-TLV has Type 14 and encodes an IPv6 node address, an SR Algorithm and an optional SRv6 SID. The Length MUST be 42 when both the SRv6 SID and the SRv6 Endpoint Behavior and SID Structure are present, 34 when only the SRv6 SID is present, or 18 when the SRv6 SID is not present. The SRv6 SID is a 16-octet address, and the value 0 MAY be used when the controller wants to indicate the desired SRv6 Endpoint Behavior or SID Structure without specifying the SID. The SRv6 Endpoint Behavior or SID Structure MUST NOT be included when the SRv6 SID has not been included.

The SR Algorithm field is 1 octet and carries the SR Algorithm as described in the Segment Routing Architecture when the A-Flag is set. When the A-Flag is not set, the field MUST be set to zero on transmission and MUST be ignored on receipt.
sections.plainLanguage: Each sub-TLV starts with a type number and a length, then a flags byte and either an algorithm number or a reserved byte. After that come the addresses that identify the step, and optionally a label or an SRv6 identifier that says how the traffic should be carried there.

sections.title: Segments That Name an Interface or a Link
sections.content:
The Type E sub-TLV has Type 5 and encodes an IPv4 node address, a local interface identifier and an optional SR-MPLS SID. The Length MUST be 14 when the SR-MPLS SID is present and 10 otherwise. The fourth octet is RESERVED, which MUST be set to zero on transmission and MUST be ignored on receipt. The Local Interface ID is 4 octets carrying the interface index of the local interface, referring to TLV 258 of RFC 9552.

The Type F sub-TLV has Type 6 and encodes an adjacency local address, an adjacency remote address and an optional SR-MPLS SID. The Length MUST be 14 when the SID is present and 10 otherwise. The Local IPv4 Address is the local link address of the node, and the Remote IPv4 Address is the link address of the neighbour node.

The Type G sub-TLV has Type 7 and encodes an IPv6 link-local adjacency for SR-MPLS, with an IPv6 local node address, a local interface identifier, an IPv6 remote node address, a remote interface identifier and an optional SR-MPLS SID. The Length MUST be 46 when the SID is present and 42 otherwise. The Remote Interface ID MAY be set to zero, and the IPv6 Remote Node Address MAY be set to zero, when the local node address and the interface identifiers are sufficient to describe the link.

The Type H sub-TLV has Type 8 and encodes an adjacency local address, an adjacency remote address and an optional SR-MPLS SID, this time with 16-octet IPv6 addresses. The Length MUST be 38 when the SID is present and 34 otherwise.

The Type J sub-TLV has Type 15 and encodes an IPv6 link-local adjacency for SRv6, with a local node address, a local interface identifier, a remote IPv6 node address, a remote interface identifier, an optional SRv6 SID and optionally the SRv6 Endpoint Behavior and SID Structure. The Length MUST be 66 when both the SID and the endpoint behavior are present, 58 when only the SID is present, or 42 when the SID is not present.

The Type K sub-TLV has Type 16 and encodes an adjacency local address, an adjacency remote address, an optional SRv6 SID and optionally the SRv6 Endpoint Behavior and SID Structure. The Length MUST be 58 when both are present, 50 when only the SID is present, or 34 when the SID is not present.

Three earlier TLV numbers, 10, 11 and 12, had been defined for the advertisement of Segment Types I, J and K in the early drafts of RFC 9830, and have been deprecated to avoid backward compatibility issues.
sections.plainLanguage: Some steps need more than an address. Types E, G and J add the index number of the interface on the router, so the step means that particular port rather than the router as a whole. Types F, H and K go further and name the link itself by giving the addresses at both of its ends.

sections.title: The Segment Flags
sections.content:
The Segment Type sub-TLVs may contain the SR Policy Segment Flags of RFC 9830 in their Flags field, and this document introduces additional flags. The Flags octet holds four flags in its top bits, in the order V, A, S and B, with the remaining bits unused.

  • The V-Flag is an existing flag defined in RFC 9830.
  • The A-Flag, when set, indicates the presence of the SR Algorithm identifier in the SR Algorithm field. The SR Algorithm is used by the Segment Routing Policy Module as described in the architecture.
  • The S-Flag, when set, indicates the presence of the SR-MPLS or SRv6 SID, depending on the segment type.
  • The B-Flag is an existing flag defined in RFC 9830.

The rules for which flag applies where are explicit. The V-Flag applies to all Segment Types, including those introduced by this document. The A-Flag applies to Segment Types C, D, I, J and K, and its value MUST be ignored for Types A, B, E, F, G and H. The S-Flag applies to Segment Types C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J and K, and its value MUST be ignored for Types A and B. The B-Flag applies to Segment Types B, I, J and K, and its value MUST be ignored for Types A, C, D, E, F, G and H.
sections.plainLanguage: The flags byte tells the receiver which optional fields are really there. Two new flags are added here: one says the algorithm number is meaningful, the other says a label or identifier is present. Each flag is only meaningful for certain segment types, and receivers are told to ignore the others.

sections.title: IANA and Security Considerations
sections.content:
IANA has allocated code points from the SR Policy Segment List Sub-TLVs registry of RFC 9830, under the Border Gateway Protocol Tunnel Encapsulation registry group: value 3 for the Type C Segment sub-TLV, 4 for Type D, 5 for Type E, 6 for Type F, 7 for Type G, 8 for Type H, 14 for Type I, 15 for Type J and 16 for Type K.

IANA has also allocated code points from the SR Policy Segment Flags registry: bit 1 for the SR Algorithm Flag, the A-Flag, and bit 2 for the SID Specified Flag, the S-Flag.

The security considerations of RFC 9830 apply to the Segment Types defined in this document, and no additional security considerations are introduced. The operations and manageability considerations of RFC 9830 likewise apply, and no additional ones are introduced.
sections.plainLanguage: The document registers the new sub-TLV numbers and the two new flag bits, and it adds nothing to the security or management rules that already apply to SR Policy in BGP.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: 3 for a Type C segment, which names an IPv4 node.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Length of the value field in octets, not counting the Type and Length fields. It is 10 with the SR-MPLS SID and 6 without.

fields.name: Flags
fields.desc: One octet of segment flags: V, A, S and B in the top four bits.

fields.name: SR Algorithm
fields.desc: The algorithm to use, meaningful only when the A-Flag is set.

fields.name: SR-MPLS SID
fields.desc: Optional: a label, Traffic Class, bottom-of-stack and TTL, as for Segment Type A.

viz.caption: THE FOUR SEGMENT FLAGS AND WHERE THEY APPLY

items.title: V-Flag
items.text: Existing flag from RFC 9830. It applies to every segment type.

items.title: A-Flag
items.text: Says the SR Algorithm field is meaningful. It applies to types C, D, I, J and K.

items.title: S-Flag
items.text: Says an SR-MPLS or SRv6 SID is present. It applies to types C through K.

items.title: B-Flag
items.text: Existing flag from RFC 9830. It applies to types B, I, J and K.
